report:
## Conclusion: The claim is false

Prolonged use of cloth or surgical face masks does **not** cause dangerous carbon-dioxide (CO₂) buildup in healthy people. This claim circulated widely during the COVID-19 pandemic and has been repeatedly debunked by direct physiological studies and fact-checkers.

**Key evidence:**

- A study published in the *Annals of the American Thoracic Society* measured gas exchange in healthy adults and in veterans with severe COPD while wearing surgical masks. It found no clinically meaningful changes in oxygen or CO₂ levels—even in patients with impaired lung function—concluding masks are "unlikely to cause over-exposure to CO₂" (https://www.eurekalert.org/news-releases/694889).

- A 2023 study measuring CO₂ directly behind and in front of surgical, cloth, and N95-style masks found that continuous mask-wearing did not produce dangerous CO₂ accumulation; CO₂ disperses through and around the mask rather than being rebreathed at toxic levels (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10324709/).

- The Associated Press confirmed the CDC never said cloth masks trap CO₂, and there is no evidence masks cause hypercapnia (dangerous blood CO₂) (https://apnews.com/article/archive-fact-checking-9101740032).

- Medical experts note CO₂ molecules are far too small to be trapped by mask fabric; any brief rise in inhaled CO₂ is trivial and quickly corrected by normal breathing (https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/factcheck/2020/05/30/fact-check-wearing-face-mask-not-cause-hypoxia-hypercapnia/5260106002/).

**Caveat:** One 2023 review hypothesized about *chronic* low-level CO₂ exposure, but it was speculative, not direct experimental evidence of harm, and contradicts measured physiological data. Masks may feel uncomfortable, but discomfort is not CO₂ poisoning.
